accuracy.evidence: Every number recomputed by hand and in the lab code: 6+8+7+5+9 = 35, 35 ÷ 5 = 7; 72+85+90+68+95 = 410, 410 ÷ 5 = 82 (median of the sorted list 68, 72, 85, 90, 95 is 85, used as the distractor); 3+5+6+8 = 22, 22 ÷ 4 = 5.5; 4+6+7+9 = 26, 26 ÷ 4 = 6.5 (÷ 5 = 5.2 distractor); 3 values with mean 10 need total 30, so 30 − 17 = 13; 9 → 24 makes the total 50 and the mean 10; 2, 0, 4 gives 6 ÷ 3 = 2; heights 128…170 total 826, mean ≈ 137.7, above five of six values. Definition (total ÷ number of values) and 'interpret the mean as an average' follow NC Year 6 statistics; CCSS 6.SP.A.3/6.SP.B.5c wording checked. Parameterised items checked at range corners: p2 4m (5..12), p4 5m − t (m 6..10, t 16..24, never below 6), m3 a + 2, m5 2m − a (≥ 12).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS2 mean errors (NCETM Year 6 statistics guidance; Watson & Moritz on 'mean as fair share'): stopping at the total (challenge tag nodiv on 410 and 26, step 2 prediction '35'); giving the median (tag median on 85, and on 'the middle child'); dividing by the wrong count (wrongn 5.2) and dropping a 0 value (zero, m2 '3'); believing the mean must be a data value or a whole number (step 3 prediction, tag isvalue, p5); assuming a missing value equals the mean (step 5 prediction '8', tag same, m7 '10'); and over-estimating an outlier's pull (step 4 prediction '22', tag jump) or ignoring it (stays).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmean is built around the mean's own mechanism: cube towers that conserve the total while you level them, a tip-and-share pile (total ÷ count), half cubes that make 5.5 visible, a stretchable outlier tower with a live mean line, and a missing-value tower with a green target-mean line. flagmad measures distances from the mean, flagstatvoc names averages, and the generic statlab drags dots; none levels cubes or shares a pile. The 6-shingle gate passes against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the mean before being told: moving cubes keeps 'Total 35 ÷ 5' fixed while towers level at 7; tipping all five towers shows the pile of 35 and Share gives 7 each, so both pictures meet at the same number; with 3, 5, 6, 8 whole cubes stop at 5, 5, 6, 6 and the narration asks for the spare cubes to be split, giving 5.5; stretching one tower by 15 moves the red mean line only from 7 to 10; the fifth tower only meets the green line at 6 because 8 × 5 = 40 and 40 − 34 = 6.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: the total 'goes up' or 'goes down' when cubes move (the readout stays 35); the mean is '35' (the pile must still be shared); the mean must be 'one of the scores' or 'the middle one' (5.5 appears); one big score makes the mean 'go up by 15, to 22' (it reaches 10); the missing score is '8, the same as the mean' (the tower meets the target at 6).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Ten distinct wrong-answer messages, each naming the slip: nodiv (that is the total, now divide), median (that is the middle value, the mean uses every value), wrongn (there are 4 values, not 5), same (the missing value need not equal the mean, total must be 30), nototal (17 is only the two you know), jump (the 15 is shared between 5), stays (the total went up so the mean did), zero (0 still counts, divide by 3), isvalue (5.5 from 3, 5, 6, 8).

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes: learner kid text FK 2.1 (limit 7.0), adult FK 6.2 (limit 10.0). Sentences are short; 'average', 'mean', 'total' and 'outlier' are each explained in plain words where first used, and every rule comes with a worked number (35 ÷ 5 = 7, 22 ÷ 4 = 5.5, 8 × 5 = 40). Lab step text is two or three short sentences and buttons say what they do (Tallest gives one to shortest, Tip score 6, Share between 5, Fifth score +1).

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases, explanation overlap with every other lesson under 12%). Kid paragraphs: the rule with a worked example; levelling towers; mean need not be a value, zeros count, outlier shares; working backwards to a missing value. Adult paragraphs: curriculum statements and the two models; named common mistakes; interpreting the mean and outliers; what each lab step does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark themes after Show me on all 6 steps. The first pass left 'Tip score 7' buttons visible after sharing and an empty canvas on challenge questions with no data; both fixed (buttons hide once shared or levelled; data-free questions show the mean rule). The dark-theme mean line was too dark red and now uses a lighter red and green. Cubes stay at least 9 px tall even when the outlier tower reaches 24; score labels sit in pills under each tower; buttons wrap two to a row.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button: Tallest gives one to shortest, Tip score n (one per tower), Share between 5, Split the spare cubes, Last score −1/+1/+5 and Fifth score −1/+1, all with aria-labels naming the action; the challenge uses buttons with 'Answer:' labels. say() updates the canvas aria-label and the visible narration after every move with the towers, total and mean. walk.cjs (desktop and iPhone 13) completes all 5 tasks with Show me, shows the challenge, axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes and there are no console errors.
